body:
Triage (first touch): `pm:on-hold`, type `Bug` (storage-contract defect, measured).

Reasoning, 2026-08-17: the durable fix lands entirely in `driver-memory` / `driver-mongodb`, which are under the maintainer's 2026-08-05 investment freeze (cross-card anchor #5499). The one live consumer divergence was already converged at the canonical binder by #8489, and the defective row shape cannot arrive over the wire (`undefined` does not survive JSON) — reproducible but **not user-reachable**, so the Bug-hold queue-return branch does not apply. Not closed, because the maintainer's 2026-08-16 ruling on #8489 explicitly designates this card as the durable follow-up.

Restart-when: closed objectstack-ai/objectstack#5499

(Earlier restart is legitimate only if the freeze ruling is narrowed on #5499 to exclude storage-contract normalization — that is a maintainer note to record there, not a seat call.)

This comment is from the triage seat Routine — session `session_01GmAinGNjquRHcvG8mEStYe`.

## Un-held — the restart condition was already satisfied nine days before it was written

Surfaced by the #12393 dev while scoping the `VALUE_ROUNDTRIP` case-set against this card's exclusion. Acting on it here because it is a queue-state decision, not a dev fix.

This card sits `pm:on-hold` with `Restart-when: … OR driver-memory / driver-mongodb come out of the #5499 investment freeze`. Measured against the anchor card's own comments:

| event | when |
|---|---|
| `driver-mongodb` unfrozen — 「5499 解冻 mongodb 相关开发,继续全速推进」 | **2026-08-11 04:34Z** |
| `driver-memory` unfrozen — 「driver-memory 也解冻,继续清剩下两行 DEBT」, with *"this card's freeze is fully dissolved … it no longer gates anything"* | **2026-08-11 11:27Z** |
| **this card's restart line written** | **2026-08-20** |

So the condition fired **nine days before the sentence that names it**. Nothing was ever going to wake this card: a restart condition is checked by looking for the event *after* the line was written, and this one was already in the past. That is precisely the failure the card's own note says the restart line was added to prevent — the line built the trap it was meant to close.

Moved to `pm:queue`. Not claimed and not dispatched in this batch; it takes its place in normal selection.

⚠️ Worth generalising rather than just fixing this instance: **a restart condition whose event may already have occurred is not a hold, it is a silent drop.** Anything writing one should check the condition's current state at the moment of writing — the same "re-verify the premise, don't inherit it" rule that applies to a card's citations applies to its restart line. Raising it here rather than filing a process card, since the mechanism is the same one #12395 / #12397 exercised correctly today by re-scanning their upstreams.

For the record, this card is also now referenced from the `VALUE_ROUNDTRIP` case-set: an explicitly-`undefined` declared field is scoped **out** of that case-set by name, with this card cited and the condition for lifting the exclusion stated in the file — not ledgered, so no new escape hatch was opened.

## Claimed and dispatched

- **Session**: `session_01W6HFzyH98W1YaQXhJUJt6o` (seat post #6367)
- **Branch**: `claude/issue-9276-driver-own-key-undefined`
- Comments re-read in the same action as the claim. No prior claim by any other session.

**The hold is discharged and the scope note is now moot.** This card's `Restart-when:` line named three exits, one of them *"`driver-memory` / `driver-mongodb` come out of the #5499 investment freeze"* — which had already happened **nine days before that line was written**, as I recorded here earlier today. The body's closing caveat — *"whether the freeze covers this is a lane call"* — is answered: there is no freeze. Both drivers are enrolled on ordinary terms.

### The fork, and where its boundary is

The card names the repair as *"either dropped from the row or returned as `null`"*. That is a real choice and it goes to the dev, because the evidence already points one way and the dev should confirm or refute it rather than inherit it: both measured consumers read an own key holding `undefined` as **absent** — CEL (`has(record.status)` is `false`) and `materializeDeclaredFields`, the latter by documented design. Dropping the key is the reading that matches what the platform already believes; returning `null` would make it a *value*, which is the one thing the two states are supposed to distinguish.

⛔ But if the repair turns into a question about **what a stored row may contain** rather than what this driver emits, that is a storage-contract question and a maintainer floor — report the fork. Same boundary the seat applied to #12397 and #12578 today.

### What must not be lost

⭐ The card's own starred note is carried into the brief verbatim, because it is the part most likely to be flattened: **a fail-OPEN consumer on this input class is a different card entirely and must not wait for this one.** The single consumer measured so far (#8489's eligibility gate in `plugin-sharing`) was fail-**closed** before and after, so nobody was over-granted — that is why this is a contract-hygiene card and not an incident. If the dev's sweep turns up a fail-open consumer, it stops being this card.

`driver-mongodb` is the other JS-backed driver in the family and the card asks for it to be measured the same way before deciding — not assumed to match `driver-memory`. `SqlDriver` cannot express the shape at all (a SQL NULL arrives as `null`, a value), so the divergence is JS-backed versus SQL-backed by construction.

Serial check: `packages/drivers/driver-memory` and `driver-mongodb`. The open #12591 holds `sql-driver.ts` only; #12578 is `packages/objectql`; #12559 is in the i18n extract configs. No overlap.

## Dispatch killed by a container restart — work recovered and pushed, **not** verified

The dev seat was killed mid-task when the container restarted. Its worktree survived; nothing had reached origin. Recovered and pushed at 17:5xZ — **1 commit**, clean tree:

```
263c74db00  fix(drivers): a declared field written as an explicit `undefined` is
            indistinguishable from one never written
```

The commit subject says the fork was answered the way the evidence pointed — **drop the key**, so the two states are indistinguishable — but there is **no PR, no gate output, no ablation, and no `driver-mongodb` measurement** in the record. The card asked for mongodb to be measured rather than assumed to match `driver-memory`, and that is not evidenced anywhere. Treat the branch as a starting point.

⭐ For whoever resumes, the starred note is still the one that must not be flattened: **a fail-OPEN consumer on this input class is a different, more urgent card and must not wait for this one.** Whether the killed dispatch's sweep turned one up is unknown — the sweep's result died with the seat, so it has to be re-run rather than presumed clean.

Second stall-and-recover on this seat today; the first is recorded on #12068 / #11671 / #12393 and in §7 of seat post #6367.
